summary: Hardened untrusted request, path and diagnostic presentation data and verified the existing test-only external-process boundary with argument vectors, bounded timeout and concurrent stdout/stderr draining.

startingState.worktree: Tracked files were clean before W12-S04 implementation; ignored campaign state had W12-S03 completed and W12-S04 planned, and campaign-state transitions were not included in the scope commit.
startingState.aheadNote: The ahead count includes reachable completed Search scope commits through W12-S03; no upstream changes were present.

implementation.scopeBoundary: Only the owning repository's Search production diagnostics, Search test-process oracle, adversarial tests and Search documentation changed, plus this scope's evidence. No sibling repository, package version, publication state or host/SQL engine source was changed.
implementation.presentationBoundary: Machine-facing paths and Search rows retain bounded source values. Diagnostic presentation has a separate escaped and bounded display form for control, format and separator characters. Request parser messages never include raw unbounded JSON, snippets or ignore content.
implementation.processBoundary: Production Search has no external-process execution. The test-only ripgrep comparator uses ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList with UseShellExecute=false, an explicit -- path boundary, concurrent stdout/stderr drains and a 30-second process-tree timeout.

scenarios: Leading-dash filename identity remains exact in Search rows.
Malicious request keys and values cannot inject control characters into diagnostic presentation.
Machine-facing diagnostic paths remain exact while DisplayPath is bounded and escaped.
The process comparator preserves the pinned ripgrep contract and explicit -- boundary.
Large simultaneous stdout and stderr streams are drained without deadlock.
Ripgrep matched, no-match, operational-error, JSON-truncation and binary-output cases remain green.

iterationDiagnostics: The first adversarial attempt confirmed that Windows rejects newline filename components; the filesystem identity test was made platform-aware while synthetic diagnostic-path coverage retained quote/newline/control cases.

gateResults.evidence: The exact Release owning-repository suite completed across 21 projects with 1,582 total tests, 1,548 passed, 0 failed and 34 classified skips; the focused Search suite and adversarial process/data tests also passed.

The separate review approved presentation separation, process ownership, bounded diagnostics, timeout cleanup and scope boundaries; exact source hashes and the unique trailer-bearing completion commit are retained.
Adversarial request-key/value, path, leading-dash, control-character, large-dual-stream and operational-process cases pass without shell interpolation or unsafe diagnostic expansion.
Source, request, completion, match and scope contract harnesses pass 27 scenarios and 314 assertions in total, and machine-facing row/path values remain exact.
Diagnostic display data is bounded and escaped, process output drains concurrently, timeout cleanup kills the process tree, and ignore text never crosses into command execution.

knownLimitations: Windows rejects newline and double-quote filename components; the platform-aware filesystem test uses a leading-dash filename while synthetic diagnostic-path coverage exercises quote/newline/control data.
Diagnostic Location.Path is bounded machine data; terminal/UI consumers must use DisplayPath for presentation safety.
Production Search does not execute external tools. The process timeout/argument-vector behavior is verified in the test-only ripgrep comparator boundary.
The repository suite retained 34 classified skips: 31 expected and 3 platform-conditional symlink skips, plus existing package-audit/compiler warnings.
No package was published, pushed, released or installed, and no sibling repository was edited.
